speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned you have gait and limb ataxia along with a significant medical history; could you please detail your past medical conditions and any specific medications you are currently taking? Additionally, do you experience any other neurological symptoms such as weakness, numbness, or changes in vision?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the "drunken" gait and right-sided clumsiness are concerning for cerebellar or spinal cord involvement. Given your significant medical history, are you currently taking any medications that might be toxic to the nervous system, such as chemotherapy agents or heavy metals? Please also confirm if you have a history of head trauma or recent infections.

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab use.

I have reached my diagnostic conclusion based on the combination of your ataxia symptoms, the "drunken" gait, and your specific history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab, which is a known risk factor for PML. No further questions or tests are required to confirm this diagnosis.
